entities.text:
Nafr
 High Court of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This is the irst bail application iled by the applicants under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail, as they have been arrested in connection with Crime No. 83/2024 registered at Police Station - Amanaka, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh for the ofences punishable under Sections 283,
420, 467, 468, 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Sections 47 (A), 54 (1), 54 (2) & 54 (3)
of the Chhattisgarh Krishi Pashu Parirakshan Adhiniyam, 1978 and under Section 11 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 and under Sections 04, 06, 07, 09, 10, 11 of the Chhattisgarh Krishak Pashu Parirakshan Adhiniyam, 2004.
2. Case of the prosecution is that, on 14.02.2024 at about 11:50 P.M. report was lodged in the concerned police station by the complainant alleging that the complainant received an information that on a Truck bearing No. KA-07-B-6331, cattles are loaded and they are being taken to slaughter house at Hyderabad.

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The complainant intercepted the truck near Kharun River Bridge, upon which,
driver of the truck led away.
Police was called and upon opening the container of the truck, 83 cattles were found loaded in the container, out of which, 11 cattles were dead.
Upon verifying the registration number of the truck, it also revealed that behind the No. KA-07-B-6331, one another number i.e. TS-12-UE-1338 was mentioned.
Aforementioned crime was registered against the unknown person.
During the course of investigation, applicants were arrested on 16.02.2024 and their memorandum statements were recorded.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that applicant are innocent, they have been falsely implicated in the instant crime, they have not committed any ofence as alleged.
He submits that the applicants are drivers of the Truck which was intercepted and found to be transporting the cattle.
He contended that they were discharging their duties on the instructions of the owner and others.
There are no other criminal antecedents against them.
They are the only earning members of their family.
They are in jail since 16.02.2024.
Charge-sheet is iled, ofence is triable by the Judicial Magistrate 1st Class.
Trial may take sometime, hence, they may be enlarged on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for applicants.
However, he do not dispute the submission of the counsel for the applicants that there are no criminal antecedent against them as also, the fact that charge- sheet is iled.
Submission of counsel for the applicants that they are are drivers is not disputed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the respective parties.

6. Taking into consideration, facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations, submission of learned counsel for the respective parties as also, that the applicants are employed as Driver,
there are no criminal antecedents against them, ofence is triable by Judicial Magistrate First Class,
charge-sheet is iled, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I am inclined to allow this application for grant of bail.

7. Accordingly, the bail application iled under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is directed that applicants shall be released on bail on each of them furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to satisfaction of Trial Court concerned on the conditions that:
(i) They shall appear before the Trial Court concerned regularly on each and every date unless exempted from appearance.
(ii) They shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) If applicants are found involved in similar ofence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of bail.
Certiied copy as per rules.
